memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user keeps a portable fan charger on a living-room shelf.
On a hot day, the user worked with only the window open and lost focus in the afternoon.
In the room where the user closed the curtains the next morning, the temperature rose less.
The user took the portable fan out without charging it, and it turned off after an hour.
Before the next outing, the user charged it the night before and used the fan throughout the trip.
On a hot weekend, the user was eating lunch in their father's yard and moved indoors.
When the user returned to the yard in the evening, shade and wind led them to stay another hour.
The user's father prefers to move an outdoor meal to the evening rather than proceed at midday when the temperature is high.
The local agent can compare past responses to heat but cannot know the current felt temperature without an indoor temperature record.
A room with a west-facing window can warm rapidly in the late afternoon.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate practical contexts. The reference frame concerns family birthday dining, conversational noise, and gathering choices, while the compared frame concerns heat management, portable-fan readiness, and timing or location changes. Neither side supplies a scope-aligned claim about the other’s decisions.
